tr: „But I'm still tired after two hours.“
en: „But I'm still tired after two hours.“

tr: Yeni daire geziliyor. Ne nerede duruyor?
en: A tour of the new flat. What stands where?

tr: „One tablet twice a day.“ — sabah bir, akşam bir.
en: „One tablet twice a day.“ — one in the morning, one in the evening.

tr: „already“ yardımcı ile asıl fiil arasında duruyor.
en: „already“ sits between the auxiliary and the main verb.

tr: Sıklık kalıbı: sayı + „times“ + „a“ + zaman birimi.
en: The frequency pattern: number + „times“ + „a“ + unit of time.

tr: Taşınma günü, adım adım. Ne bitti, ne henüz bitmedi?
en: Moving day, step by step. What is done and what is not done yet?

tr: Varlık sorusunda „is there“ tekil, „are there“ çoğul.
en: In an existence question „is there“ is singular and „are there“ is plural.

tr: Önce danışma, sonra kuyruk, sonra sigorta, en son oda.
en: First the information desk, then the queue, then the insurance, and the room last.

tr: „You can get tired. Don't drive in the first two days.“
en: „You can get tired. Don't drive in the first two days.“

tr: „I exercise three times a week.“ — ayda iki kez olan et.
en: „I exercise three times a week.“ — the meat is what comes twice a month.

tr: Dört daire, dört kusur. Sonunda seçilen en güzeli değil.
en: Four flats, four faults. The one chosen in the end is not the finest.

tr: Gürültü şikâyeti, üç adımda. Sonuncusu pastayla bitiyor.
en: A noise complaint in three steps. The last one ends with cake.

tr: İki arıza bildiriliyor. Hangisi ne zamandan beri sürüyor?
en: Two faults are reported. Which one has lasted since when?

tr: Mülakat öncesi. Kim neyden endişeli, kim neyden korkuyor?
en: Before the interview. Who is worried about what, and who is afraid of what?

tr: „Twenty. That is ten days.“ — günde iki tane, on gün eder.
en: „Twenty. That is ten days.“ — two a day makes ten days.

tr: Şikâyetin kibar açılışı; asıl konu „but“tan sonra geliyor.
en: The polite opening of a complaint; the real subject comes after „but“.

tr: „Gone since Tuesday.“ — cuma soğuk algınlığının başlangıcı.
en: „Gone since Tuesday.“ — Friday is where the cold began.

tr: Doz ve sıklık cümlelerini yaz. Sonunda ilaç kartını doldur.
en: Write the sentences about dose and frequency. Then fill in the medicine card.

tr: Kısa sıfat „-er“ alıyor ve iki taraf „than“ ile bağlanıyor.
en: The short adjective takes „-er“ and the two sides are joined with „than“.

tr: Metin birinciden dördüncüye doğru gidiyor; alınan sonuncusu.
en: The text runs from the first to the fourth; the one taken is the last.

tr: Bir sabah, üç masa: danışma, servis, sigorta. Ne gerekiyordu?
en: One morning, three desks: information, ward, insurance. What was needed?

tr: İyileşme konuşması. Kim hangi süreyi söylüyor, hangisi doğru?
en: A talk about getting better. Who names which length of time, and which one is right?

tr: „Because I sleep there.“ — birincide sokak pencerenin altında.
en: „Because I sleep there.“ — in the first one the street is under the window.

tr: „We haven't turned on the electricity yet…“ — ışık telefondan.
en: „We haven't turned on the electricity yet…“ — the light comes from the phone.

tr: Arızayı bildir. Süren bozukluk olumsuz present perfect istiyor.
en: Report the fault. A defect that is still going asks for the negative present perfect.

tr: „…it has been there since Saturday.“ — pazartesi kalorifere ait.
en: „…it has been there since Saturday.“ — Monday belongs to the heating.

tr: „First…“, „After that…“ ve saatler sırayı metnin içinde veriyor.
en: „First…“, „After that…“ and the times give the order inside the text itself.

tr: Evi anlat ve daireyi sor. Karşılaştırma burada betimleme işinde.
en: Describe the home and ask about the flat. Comparison is doing descriptive work here.

tr: „He came on Tuesday, looked at the pipe and said: I can't fix it.“
en: „He came on Tuesday, looked at the pipe and said: I can't fix it.“

tr: Taşınmayı sırayla anlat. „yet“ ve „since“ henüz bitmemişi taşıyor.
en: Tell the move in order. „yet“ and „since“ carry what is not finished.

tr: His cümleleri. Her sıfatın kendi edatı var; ezberlenecek yer orası.
en: Sentences about feelings. Every adjective has its own preposition; that is the part to learn by heart.

tr: „…the advert said „furnished“ and there was only a bed and a table.“
en: „…the advert said „furnished“ and there was only a bed and a table.“

tr: Sıradan bir hafta. Sıklık zarfları ve „times a week“ kalıbı bir arada.
en: An ordinary week. Frequency adverbs and the „times a week“ pattern together.

tr: „A woman gave us a form and asked for a signature.“ — para eczane için.
en: „A woman gave us a form and asked for a signature.“ — the money is for the pharmacy.

tr: Sigorta ve bekleme soruları. Sonuncusu ünitenin asıl işi: dolaylı soru.
en: Questions about insurance and waiting. The last one is the unit's real job: the indirect question.

tr: „…there are two shelves on the wall.“ — tekili „shelf“, çoğulu „shelves“.
en: „…there are two shelves on the wall.“ — singular „shelf“, plural „shelves“.

tr: „No, only the patients show a card.“ — kart hastanın, ziyaretçinin değil.
en: „No, only the patients show a card.“ — the card belongs to the patient, not to the visitor.

tr: Kutunun üstündeki talimat konuşuluyor. Kaç tane, ne zaman, yan etkisi ne?
en: The instructions on the box are discussed. How many, when, and what side effect?

tr: Deniz üç gün diyor, Ela düzeltiyor: „Almost a week. It started on Friday.“
en: Deniz says three days and Ela corrects that: „Almost a week. It started on Friday.“

tr: Bir daire tek tek anlatılıyor. Hangi oda daha aydınlık, hangisi daha rahat?
en: A flat is described piece by piece. Which room is brighter, and which is more comfortable?

tr: „The first week I said nothing.“ — yukarı çıkmak ikinci, mektup üçüncü adım.
en: „The first week I said nothing.“ — going up is the second step, the letter the third.

tr: „The heating hasn't worked since Monday.“ — cumartesi sızıntının başlangıcı.
en: „The heating hasn't worked since Monday.“ — Saturday is where the leak began.

tr: „I'm afraid of the questions.“ — para sorusu ayrı, orada „worried about“ diyor.
en: „I'm afraid of the questions.“ — the money question is separate, and there it says „worried about“.

tr: „Two men carried the cupboard up the stairs and it didn't go through the door.“
en: „Two men carried the cupboard up the stairs and it didn't go through the door.“

tr: Dolaylı soruda sıra DÜZ cümle gibi: „where I can find“, „where can I find“ değil.
en: In an indirect question the order stays STATEMENT order: „where I can find“, not „where can I find“.

tr: „I haven't heard the music since August.“ — olumsuz present perfect: o günden beri hiç.
en: „I haven't heard the music since August.“ — negative present perfect: not once since that day.
